summary: Defines a Media Gateway Control Protocol package for supporting fax calls. It allows two approaches: using ITU-T T.38 fax relay under the control of the Call Agent, or letting the gateway choose a fax transmission method and handle the call without involving the Call Agent. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Fax machines still need to work over the internet. This explains two ways the phone-network gateways can handle a fax: following the boss's detailed orders, or deciding by themselves.

subtitle: Controlling fax calls through MGCP gateways with T.38 relay or gateway autonomy.

tldr.problem: Fax machines and modems need special handling over IP networks because audio codecs designed for voice perform poorly with fax tones and data signals.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5347 defines an MGCP package that allows Call Agents to request T.38 fax relay (using ITU-T Recommendation T.38), allow gateways to choose their own fax handling method, or disable special fax handling entirely, with events to notify the Call Agent when fax is detected.
tldr.outcome: Gateways can support fax calls reliably either under Call Agent control or autonomously, enabling voice-over-IP systems to interwork with the PSTN for fax service.

facts.label: Call Agent control modes
facts.value: T.38 strict, T.38 loose, gateway, off

today: RFC 5347 is Informational and defines a standard MGCP package for fax support that remains widely used in VoIP gateway implementations. The two-mode architecture accommodates both centrally controlled and autonomously intelligent gateways.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Fax machines are part of business communications even in the age of internet calling, and VoIP gateways must seamlessly interconnect them with IP-based systems. Standard audio codecs optimized for voice (such as G.711 or G.729) perform poorly with fax signals, leading to failed transmissions or low quality transfers. ITU-T Recommendation T.38 specifies a specialized protocol for transmitting fax data over IP networks using UDP or TCP.

RFC 5347 defines an MGCP package to enable Media Gateway Control Protocol gateways to support fax calls in two fundamentally different ways. The first approach uses T.38 fax relay under the control of a Call Agent (the software component that controls the gateway and mediates between voice protocols like SIP and the gateway's control interface). The second approach lets the gateway itself decide upon a fax handling method without Call Agent involvement, optimizing local decisions based on capabilities it knows about both endpoints.
sections.eli5: Fax doesn't work well over the internet like voice does. MGCP is the protocol that controls internet phone gateways. This RFC explains two ways to handle fax: the controller tells the gateway what to do, or the gateway figures it out itself.

sections.title: Fax Handling Procedures
sections.content:
The fax package defines four primary fax handling procedures. T.38 Strict mode means the Call Agent controls use of T.38 fax relay, and the gateway will only attempt T.38 if it has received capability information from the remote side indicating T.38 support. T.38 Loose mode is similar but does not require confirmation of remote T.38 support, allowing the gateway to attempt T.38 even if the remote side has not explicitly advertised support.

Gateway mode allows the gateway to autonomously detect fax and decide what to do, whether that is using T.38, another method, or no special handling. The gateway notifies the Call Agent of its decision via events. Off mode disables special fax handling, though the gateway may still adjust local echo cancellation and switch to an alternative codec if needed.

The Call Agent supplies preference-ordered lists of procedures to the gateway; the gateway selects the first one it can support given the remote side's capabilities. If multiple options are provided, the gateway skips procedures that cannot be supported and chooses the highest-preference option that can work.
sections.eli5: Strict T.38: only switch if the other side says it supports T.38. Loose T.38: try T.38 anyway. Gateway mode: the gateway decides. Off: don't do anything special. Give it a list in order and it picks the first one that works.

sections.title: Call Agent Control vs. Gateway Autonomy
sections.content:
In T.38 Strict or Loose modes, the Call Agent controls the timing and details of the switch to fax. When the gateway detects fax (based on V.21 fax preamble or optionally T.30 CNG tone), it generates a t38(start) event and waits for the Call Agent to issue a ModifyConnection command instructing the switch to image/t38 media format. Only after receiving this instruction does the gateway actually switch the media stream, allowing the Call Agent to coordinate both sides of the connection simultaneously.

In Gateway mode, the gateway handles the decision autonomously. If it initiates special fax handling, it generates a gwfax(start) event. If negotiation results in no special fax handling despite a fax call being detected, it generates a nopfax(start) event. The Call Agent must respect this autonomy and refrain from issuing conflicting commands while the gateway is handling fax. Gateway mode is ideal when the gateway has local knowledge about both endpoints and can make better decisions than a remote Call Agent.
sections.eli5: Call Agent control: gateway says "fax detected" and waits for orders before switching. Gateway mode: gateway says "I'll handle this fax my way" and does it automatically. Call Agent responds to events, doesn't give orders.

sections.title: Fax Detection and Event Reporting
sections.content:
Gateways detect fax calls by recognizing specific signals. The V.21 fax preamble (used by the ITU-T T.30 fax protocol) is the most reliable indicator and is mandatory for implementations. Triggering on T.30 CNG (Calling Tone) is optional but common; however, when T.38 version 2 or earlier is used (which does not support V.34 high-speed modulation), CNG-based detection can cause V.34 faxes to downspeed to G3 speeds.

When fax is detected and special handling is invoked, the gateway generates events with start, stop, and failure parameters. For T.38 modes, the Call Agent receives the t38(start) event and must coordinate both ends of the connection to switch media. The Call Agent may need to abort an in-progress T.38 procedure by instructing the gateway to use the off fax mode, allowing fallback to audio codecs if T.38 fails.

The RFC defines rules for procedure selection, parameter negotiation with RFC 3407 SDP capability descriptions, and implementation considerations such as maintaining the same IP address and port when switching between audio and T.38, and accepting case-insensitive encodings of T.38 attributes.
sections.eli5: Listen for fax beeps and special signals. When you hear one, send an event to the Call Agent. Switch media formats only after getting permission. If T.38 fails, go back to voice.

sections.title: Call Flow Examples
sections.content:
RFC 5347 provides detailed call flow examples showing how T.38 Strict mode works end-to-end. The originating Call Agent creates a connection with PCMU audio and requests T.38 strict fax handling. The terminating Call Agent creates a matching connection with the same SDP, indicating both sides support T.38. When the terminating fax machine answers with T.30 CED tones and V.21 preamble, the terminating gateway generates a t38(start) event.

The terminating Call Agent responds by issuing a ModifyConnection command to switch to image/t38 media. It also sends a re-INVITE to the originating Call Agent with updated SDP. The originating Call Agent issues a matching ModifyConnection to its gateway, and once both sides switch to T.38, fax transmission proceeds. When the fax completes, either side's gateway generates a t38(stop) event, allowing the Call Agent to revert to audio if needed.

Additional examples demonstrate handling multiple and different fax options on the two sides, and interaction with SIP endpoints that may not support T.38, requiring fallback to audio-based fax passthrough.
sections.eli5: Call Agent says "switch to T.38 if fax starts." When fax is detected, the gateway alerts the Call Agent. Call Agent tells both ends to switch media. Fax sends and receives through T.38. When done, everything switches back to voice.
